definitions.explanation: The area or ground immediately around or beneath one's feet.
The stability or condition of one's stance.
Figuratively, a vulnerability that can be exploited.

examples.japanese: {足元|あしもと}に{気|き}をつけてください。
{暗|くら}いから{足元|あしもと}が{見|み}えない。
examples.english: It's dark, so I can't see where I'm stepping.

examples.japanese: {足元|あしもと}を{見|み}られている。
examples.english: They're taking advantage of my weakness.

notes:
USAGE: {足元|あしもと} has both literal and figurative meanings.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{足元|あしもと}に{気|き}をつける (to watch one's step)
・{足元|あしもと}がおぼつかない (to be unsteady on one's feet)
・{足元|あしもと}を{見|み}る (to exploit someone's weakness)
・{足元|あしもと}にも{及|およ}ばない (to not hold a candle to; to be far inferior)

WRITING VARIATIONS: Can also be written as {足下|あしもと}.

RELATED:
・{足場|あしば} - foothold, scaffold
・{地面|じめん} - ground
